items.summary: agent-autoloop is an open-source AI agent skill designed to let your command line agent operate autonomously in the background, handling tasks independently until it encounters something it's unsure about, at which point it sends a card to you for decision-making. It's a lightweight automation hub that decouples task scheduling, event sources, agents, notification channels, and even code deployment pipelines into easily swappable plugins. This setup allows for self-contained operation on your Mac or Linux without needing cloud services or public network ports. It has 2,748 GitHub stars and is verified by SkillsLLM.

items.title: sand3d
items.description: 3D modeling in Python, built for LLMs.
items.summary: sand3d is a new open-source Python library designed for 3D modeling, specifically built for large language models (LLMs). It allows an AI model to write a 3D object as a short program, described in a few hundred tokens, detailing profiles, solids, edits, joints, and assemblies. This approach enables a model to generate the code quickly, and the resulting 3D file is usable and runs over Blender's engine. The library is not just for static shapes but also handles moving joints and parts. It turns Blender into a text-based toolkit where a language model writes a few simple lines to create complex machines, like a washing machine, in under forty lines.

items.title: vork
items.description: Headless 3D and VFX engine for agents. Research preview.
items.summary: Vork is a headless 3D and VFX engine for agents, written in Rust and Slang, with GPU rendering through Vulkan and Metal. It is a research preview, source-available and free during the preview period. The engine allows agents to write scenes as code, render them, and revise the code based on the results. It features a path tracer, but it is noted to be slower than Cycles. The engine is currently limited, with fog and volumes not yet implemented, heavy interiors potentially aborting on Mac, and performance issues. The default rendering combines raster visibility with hardware ray-traced lighting and a path tracer. The cache is located under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\\vork` on Windows. To install, use `py -m pip install "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\\Programs\\vork\\python"` and `npm install "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\\Programs\\vork\\sdk"`. The native executable should be kept on PATH. For source builds, refer to `vork help build`.

items.summary: GPU Taskman is a terminal tool described as a GPU task manager for Windows, Linux, and WSL, providing per-process VRAM, GPU activity, and LLM model and KV-cache insights. It is associated with Microsoft engineer Scott Hanselman and aims to answer the question of what is using a user's GPU memory. The project is MIT-licensed and compares itself to a classic Unix tool, calling itself “An `htop` for what’s inside your GPU, not just how full it is.” The sources do not provide specific details on the exact version or date of the tool's release.

items.title: poki
items.description: Let AI agents operate a real iPhone. Local MCP server and agent, no jailbreak, no extra hardware.
items.summary: Poki is an open-source project that allows AI agents to operate a real iPhone without jailbreaking or installing any apps. It runs as a local MCP server and connects to AI agents like Codex or Claude Code to perform actions such as tapping, swiping, and typing. Poki uses Apple’s device developer services to directly control the iPhone, eliminating the need for test apps or external hardware. It requires a Mac to run and supports wireless operation on the same local network. The project is still early, with under 450 stars and needs the Mac to remain powered on to function. Real-device operations are currently slow, with each tap taking around 8 seconds and filling an input box taking about 15 seconds.

items.title: hermes-voice
items.description: Talk to a Hermes Agent profile through Home Assistant Assist
items.summary: The sources indicate that the Hermes-Voice integration allows Home Assistant to communicate with the Hermes Agent server over WebSocket, enabling Hermes to function as a native conversation agent in Home Assistant. This setup facilitates a full voice loop from wake word to speech-to-text (STT) via Hermes, then text-to-speech (TTS) back to the speaker. The integration registers a Home Assistant Assist conversation agent (`HermesConversationAgent`) on the `Platform.CONVERSATION` platform, handling both incoming `assist_query` and outgoing `assist_response` WebSocket messages. Without proper Hermes Agent server handling of these message types, conversation queries time out after 45 seconds.

items.title: agent_skills

items.title: adobe-air-desktop-tool
items.description: Adobe AIR SDK for Windows: Build Cross-Platform Desktop Apps with AJAX, HTML, and Flash
items.summary: Adobe AIR is a desktop software development tool for Windows that lets developers build standalone applications using AJAX, HTML, and Flash. It provides a runtime environment that executes rich internet applications directly on the desktop, eliminating the need for a browser while preserving web-based workflows. Cross-platform support enables a single codebase to target multiple operating systems, and the runtime is optimized for low resource consumption. The AIR SDK allows developers to create applications on a variety of desktop platforms, enabling rapid development, including animations created via Adobe Animate, and supports the deployment of applications on both desktop and mobile platforms. The project is distributed as a free download for Windows, and its maintainers assume responsibility for its development and support.
